exposure: immigrant women originating from conflict-zone countries
country of origin (Somalia, Iraq, Afghanistan, Kosovo)
cohort: First-time mothers who gave birth at Baerum Hospital in Norway between 2006-2010, including 278 women from Somalia, 166 from Iraq, 71 from Afghanistan, 67 from Kosovo, and 6,826 ethnic Norwegians
finding: Immigrant women from Somalia had the highest risk for adverse obstetric outcomes compared to other immigrant groups and ethnic Norwegians, including increased odds of emergency cesarean section, postterm birth, meconium-stained liquor, and having a small-for-gestational-age infant.
mod_finding: Immigrant women from Somalia had a lower likelihood of epidural analgesia and a higher risk of emergency cesarean section compared to ethnic Norwegians.
